one_liner: Staged, typed OCaml parser combinators (MetaOCaml) that beat ocamlyacc/ocamllex throughput on 4 of 5 grammars.
what_it_does: A parser-combinator library for OCaml whose combinator values are statically typed and type-checked for grammar ambiguity and left-recursion before use, then compiled via BER MetaOCaml multi-stage programming into specialized native parsing code. It replaces the ocamlyacc/ocamllex two-tool workflow (separate .mll/.mly grammar files) with parsers written directly in OCaml/MetaOCaml source using a combinator API (Parse(Token).type_check, then Parser(S).compile). It is not a drop-in for existing .mly/.mll grammars; you rewrite the grammar as combinators and add a MetaOCaml staging step.
how_it_is_fast: Combinators build a first-order GADT-typed grammar representation that is type-checked for unambiguity and absence of left-recursion, which guarantees linear-time, single-token-lookahead, backtrack-free parsing. Multi-stage programming (BER MetaOCaml brackets/escapes) then specializes the generic combinator interpreter into a flat, mutually-recursive first-order program per grammar, using CPS-based binding-time improvements, 'the Trick', and type-directed branch pruning (FIRST/NULL sets) to eliminate the combinator-dispatch and redundant-peek overhead present in the unstaged version.
when_to_use: Grammar is unambiguous, non-left-recursive, and parseable with one token of lookahead (arith expressions, PGN, S-expressions measured 31-75% faster than ocamlyacc/ocamllex)
Throughput on MB/s-scale character streams matters more than avoiding a new toolchain
Willing to adopt BER MetaOCaml and write parsers as staged combinator code instead of .mly/.mll grammar files
Want static rejection of ambiguous or left-recursive grammars at type-check time rather than at ocamlyacc build time
Research/prototype context where vendoring a small, peer-reviewed artifact (PLDI'19 Distinguished Artifact Award) is acceptable
when_not_to_use: String/JSON-heavy grammars: staged asp measured ~25% slower than ocamlyacc on JSON (60.32 vs 80.42 MB/s) due to per-character string handling overhead
Can't add BER MetaOCaml to the build; it is a distinct OCaml variant/toolchain, not stock OCaml plus opam
Need an actively maintained library: last commit 2025-05-16, and the repo has received only toolchain-compatibility updates since 2019
Need the unstaged/plain-combinator form for simplicity: it is 4.5-125x slower than ocamlyacc (as low as <1% of ocamlyacc's JSON throughput), so only the staged path is usable in production
Need backtracking or ambiguous-grammar support: the type system deliberately forbids ambiguous and left-recursive grammars

integration.dependencies: letrec (metaocaml-letrec); the BER MetaOCaml compiler itself
integration.min_toolchain: BER MetaOCaml (paper benchmarks used N107; current opam/README target the 4.11.1+BER switch; closed issues show added support for N111 and N153); not plain OCaml
integration.platforms: not documented beyond the paper's test machine (AMD FX 8320, Debian Linux); no explicit platform restriction in source
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — combinator API in OCaml/MetaOCaml source (Parse(Token).type_check, Parser(S).compile), not a .mly/.mll grammar-file replacement

gotchas: type_check rejects ambiguous or left-recursive grammars outright with no backtracking fallback, so some grammars simply cannot be expressed
Parser(S).compile returns a MetaOCaml `code` value, not a ready function; it must be run through MetaOCaml staging/execution, an extra step versus ocamlyacc's directly generated .ml
the Unstaged module (same combinators, no staging) is 4.5-125x slower than ocamlyacc per the paper, so don't use it expecting usable performance
string-heavy tokens (e.g. JSON) go through per-char list conversion, which the paper identifies as the specific cause of the JSON slowdown; still unfixed as of the last commit
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The sibling entries (RapidProto, Zserio, FlatBuffers, vtprotobuf) all beat protoc on serialization codegen, a different problem from asp's parser-combinator-vs-ocamlyacc/ocamllex target, so none is a substitute. Pick asp only when the real baseline is ocamlyacc/ocamllex, the grammar is unambiguous/LL(1), and BER MetaOCaml is acceptable in the build.
verified_claims_summary: Verified directly in the PLDI'19 paper (Figure 8, Section 7): staged asp combinators, compiled with BER MetaOCaml N107 and run on an AMD FX 8320/16GB Debian machine via Core_bench (95% CIs), beat ocamlyacc/ocamllex throughput on 4 of 5 benchmarks (arith 14.31 vs 10.96 MB/s, pgn 33.26 vs 21.29, ppm 11.83 vs 6.75 — the paper states 75% for PPM, sexp 43.65 vs 28.6) but lose on json, 60.32 vs 80.42 MB/s (~25% slower). Exact ocamlopt/compiler flags used for the benchmark build are not stated in the paper.
status_note: Stale: last commit 2025-05-16 was toolchain-compatibility only, and all 6 closed issues concern supporting newer BER MetaOCaml releases, not fixes or features. MIT-licensed and small enough to vendor, with a Docker-based PLDI artifact, but depends on the niche BER MetaOCaml toolchain rather than stock OCaml.
